<span class="normal">1130</span></pre></div></td><td class="code"><div><pre><span></span><span class="c1">### ==== SHARED HELPER: CLUSTER/CONSOLIDATE + NAMED SPECIAL DEMAND ====</span>
<span class="c1">#</span>
<span class="c1"># Wraps depot.demand.DemandData methods (imported, never edited - src/depot is</span>
<span class="c1"># off-limits per this project's CLAUDE.md) for two steps used by</span>
<span class="c1"># generate_demand_qzm_local.py's enrich_demand() - called either as part of</span>
<span class="c1"># the full pipeline (all()) or standalone (demand()), both via</span>
<span class="c1"># run_demand_pipeline.py:</span>
<span class="c1">#</span>
<span class="c1">#   cluster_and_consolidate(demand): merge_identical_commutes -&gt; agglomerate_pops</span>
<span class="c1">#     -&gt; cluster_points -&gt; enforce_max_pop_size. No external data - just</span>
<span class="c1">#     cleanup of whatever demand already has (fixes tiny overlapping points</span>
<span class="c1">#     and uniform-looking pop sizes).</span>
<span class="c1">#</span>
<span class="c1">#   add_named_special_demand(demand, entries): calls add_points() once per</span>
<span class="c1">#     entry from the per-city "special_demand" list (see special_demand_utils.py</span>
<span class="c1">#     and bbox_utils.py). Only entries with a non-null total_capacity should be</span>
<span class="c1">#     passed in.</span>
<span class="c1">#</span>
<span class="c1">#   route_new_pops(demand, osrm_url): resolves drivingSeconds/drivingDistance</span>
<span class="c1">#     for whatever pops add_points() just created (they always start at 0).</span>
<span class="c1">#     Deliberately does NOT use depot's own demand.calculate_routes() - see</span>
<span class="c1">#     the big comment above that function for why.</span>
<span class="c1">#</span>
<span class="c1"># NOTE on cluster_points(): its default max_pop_threshold/buffer_meters are</span>
<span class="c1"># plain Python lists, and depot's implementation indexes them with a numpy</span>
<span class="c1"># boolean mask, which crashes regardless of numpy version. We work around this</span>
<span class="c1"># entirely from the caller side (passing the same values as np.array()) rather</span>
<span class="c1"># than editing src/depot.</span>
<span class="c1">#</span>
<span class="c1"># NOTE on step order (agglomerate_pops BEFORE cluster_points, not after):</span>
<span class="c1"># agglomerate_pops() groups small residential pops *by job destination* and</span>
<span class="c1"># creates a brand-new "SO_" (super-origin) point per (job destination,</span>
<span class="c1"># spatial sub-cluster) - so the same tight-knit residential block generates</span>
<span class="c1"># one new SO_ point for every distinct job hub its residents commute to, all</span>
<span class="c1"># sitting at roughly the same physical spot. If cluster_points() already ran</span>
<span class="c1"># by that point, none of those freshly-created SO_ points ever get a chance</span>
<span class="c1"># to be spatially re-merged with each other - they're new, so cluster_points</span>
<span class="c1"># never sees them. That's exactly what caused huge numbers of small circles</span>
<span class="c1"># stacked on top of each other in dense neighborhoods even after clustering</span>
<span class="c1"># supposedly ran. Running agglomerate_pops() first, then letting</span>
<span class="c1"># cluster_points() have the last word over the *entire* resulting point set</span>
<span class="c1"># (SO_ points included), lets it re-consolidate same-block SO_ points that</span>
<span class="c1"># still overlap. Verified with a synthetic test: 100 tightly-clustered</span>
<span class="c1"># buildings feeding 5 different job hubs collapsed to 6 overlapping points</span>
<span class="c1"># with the old order, vs. 1 correctly-merged point with this order.</span>

<span class="kn">import</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nn">math</span>
<span class="kn">import</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nn">random</span>

<span class="kn">import</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nn">numpy</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">as</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nn">np</span>
<span class="kn">import</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nn">requests</span>
<span class="kn">from</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nn">concurrent.futures</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">ThreadPoolExecutor</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">as_completed</span>
<span class="kn">from</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nn">scipy.spatial</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">cKDTree</span>
<span class="kn">from</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nn">shapely.geometry</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">Point</span>


<span class="k">class</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">GreenSpaceIndex</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="sd">"""</span>
<span class="sd">    Spatial index over green-space polygons (park/nature_reserve/water_park/</span>
<span class="sd">    recreation_ground/theme_park/zoo/aquarium/national_park boundaries - see</span>
<span class="sd">    generate_demand_qzm_local.py's _capture_green_space_polygon()/</span>
<span class="sd">    capture_green_space_relations()) so coordinates WE generate after OSM</span>
<span class="sd">    parsing - split siblings from enforce_max_point_size(), or depot's own</span>
<span class="sd">    agglomerate_pops() SO_ centroids - can be checked against real terrain,</span>
<span class="sd">    not just against how close they are to other points. The OSM-extraction</span>
<span class="sd">    path already pushes park/nature_reserve ways themselves to their</span>
<span class="sd">    boundary edge (see _green_space_edge_location()), but that only covers</span>
<span class="sd">    points generated DIRECTLY from those ways - it has no way to stop</span>
<span class="sd">    something generated later (e.g. by depot's own code) from landing in</span>
<span class="sd">    the same polygon. Real case this fixes: Tempelhofer Feld, a huge</span>
<span class="sd">    mostly-empty former airport field in Berlin, where split placements and</span>
<span class="sd">    SO_ centroids had nothing stopping them from drifting into the middle</span>
<span class="sd">    of it.</span>

<span class="sd">    Only exposes containment checks - no longer a "push just outside the</span>
<span class="sd">    boundary" method. An earlier version had one (push_outside()), but</span>
<span class="sd">    nudging every offending point to its nearest boundary spot means many</span>
<span class="sd">    unrelated points scattered across one big park (e.g. several different</span>
<span class="sd">    SO_ centroids inside Tempelhofer Feld) all converge on roughly the same</span>
<span class="sd">    edge location, reproducing the exact overlapping-clusters look this was</span>
<span class="sd">    meant to fix - just moved onto the park's boundary instead of its</span>
<span class="sd">    interior. See _merge_points_in_green_space() and _place_split_point()'s</span>
<span class="sd">    green-space fallback: both now fold an offending point's population</span>
<span class="sd">    into an already-valid neighbor instead of moving it anywhere.</span>

<span class="sd">    A coarse grid of polygon bounding boxes avoids checking every candidate</span>
<span class="sd">    point against every polygon (a city can have thousands of these).</span>
<span class="sd">    Parameter/return order is (lon, lat) throughout, matching how</span>
<span class="sd">    enrich_utils.py's other placement code (_place_split_point, etc.)</span>
<span class="sd">    already works with coordinates.</span>
<span class="sd">    """</span>
    <span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="fm">__init__</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">polygons</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">cell_deg</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mf">0.01</span><span class="p">):</span>
        <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">polygons</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">polygons</span>
        <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cell_deg</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">cell_deg</span>
        <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cells</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{}</span>
        <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">poly</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="nb">enumerate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">polygons</span><span class="p">):</span>
            <span class="n">minx</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">miny</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">maxx</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">maxy</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">poly</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">bounds</span>
            <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">cx</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="nb">range</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">minx</span> <span class="o">//</span> <span class="n">cell_deg</span><span class="p">),</span> <span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">maxx</span> <span class="o">//</span> <span class="n">cell_deg</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">):</span>
                <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">cy</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="nb">range</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">miny</span> <span class="o">//</span> <span class="n">cell_deg</span><span class="p">),</span> <span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">maxy</span> <span class="o">//</span> <span class="n">cell_deg</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">):</span>
                    <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cells</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">setdefault</span><span class="p">((</span><span class="n">cx</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">cy</span><span class="p">),</span> <span class="p">[])</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">append</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">_candidates</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">):</span>
        <span class="n">cx</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">cy</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span> <span class="o">//</span> <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cell_deg</span><span class="p">),</span> <span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lat</span> <span class="o">//</span> <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cell_deg</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">seen</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">[]</span>
        <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">dx</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">):</span>
            <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">dy</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">):</span>
                <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">idx</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cells</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">get</span><span class="p">((</span><span class="n">cx</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">dx</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">cy</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">dy</span><span class="p">),</span> <span class="p">[]):</span>
                    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">idx</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">seen</span><span class="p">:</span>
                        <span class="n">seen</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">append</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">seen</span>

    <span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">containing_polygon</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">):</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="sd">"""Returns the polygon containing (lon, lat), or None."""</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">polygons</span><span class="p">:</span>
            <span class="k">return</span> <span class="kc">None</span>
        <span class="n">pt</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">Point</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">idx</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">_candidates</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">):</span>
            <span class="n">poly</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">polygons</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span>
            <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">poly</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">contains</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">pt</span><span class="p">):</span>
                <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">poly</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="kc">None</span>


<span class="c1"># depot's own documented defaults for cluster_points(), just coerced to numpy</span>
<span class="c1"># arrays to dodge the list-indexing bug described above.</span>
<span class="n">CLUSTER_MAX_POP_THRESHOLD</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">array</span><span class="p">([</span><span class="mi">25</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">75</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">200</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">500</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">5000</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">15000</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">inf</span><span class="p">])</span>
<span class="c1"># Halved from depot's own documented defaults ([1500, 1000, 500, 250, 200,</span>
<span class="c1"># 150, 125, 100]) - cluster_points() now runs AFTER agglomerate_pops() (see</span>
<span class="c1"># the module comment above), so it has the last word over the *whole* point</span>
<span class="c1"># set instead of just the original raw points. At the original buffer sizes</span>
<span class="c1"># that made it merge far more aggressively city-wide than intended - point</span>
<span class="c1"># count on a real Berlin run dropped from ~30,000 to ~2,100, producing a</span>
<span class="c1"># smaller number of very large (5k-18k) points instead of many small, spread</span>
<span class="c1"># out ones. Smaller buffers keep the *fix* (no more same-block SO_ points</span>
<span class="c1"># stacked on each other) without also flattening genuinely distinct nearby</span>
<span class="c1"># points into one.</span>
<span class="n">CLUSTER_BUFFER_METERS</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">array</span><span class="p">([</span><span class="mi">750</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">500</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">250</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">150</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">75</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">60</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">])</span>


<span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">_is_job_point</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">point</span><span class="p">):</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="sd">"""</span>
<span class="sd">    Classifies a point as job-type (True) or residential-type (False) for</span>
<span class="sd">    the purposes of applying separate job/residential tuning - see</span>
<span class="sd">    RES_SIZE_RATIO/JOB_SIZE_RATIO in generate_demand_qzm_local.py. Every</span>
<span class="sd">    point is pure one or the other when first created (job hubs get</span>
<span class="sd">    residents=0, residential hubs get jobs=0); ties (jobs == residents,</span>
<span class="sd">    including both 0) go to residential, matching agglomerate_pops()'s own</span>
<span class="sd">    SO_ points, which are always residential-only. A genuinely mixed point</span>
<span class="sd">    can only occur if some earlier step merged a job and residential point</span>
<span class="sd">    together (rare - see _merge_points_in_green_space()'s docstring) or from</span>
<span class="sd">    a special-demand landmark's own residential_split; whichever side</span>
<span class="sd">    dominates decides which cap applies.</span>
<span class="sd">    """</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">point</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"jobs"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">point</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"residents"</span><span class="p">]</span>


<span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">cluster_and_consolidate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">,</span>
                             <span class="n">agglomerate_small_threshold</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span>
                             <span class="c1"># Halved from depot's own documented defaults</span>
                             <span class="c1"># (0.03 / 0.015, ~3.3km / ~1.6km) for the same</span>
                             <span class="c1"># reason as CLUSTER_BUFFER_METERS above - these</span>
                             <span class="c1"># decide how far apart same-job-destination</span>
                             <span class="c1"># residential flows can be and still fold into</span>
                             <span class="c1"># one super-origin point.</span>
                             <span class="n">agglomerate_distance_noncbd</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mf">0.01</span><span class="p">,</span>
                             <span class="n">agglomerate_distance_cbd</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mf">0.006</span><span class="p">,</span>
                             <span class="n">cbd_bbox</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">,</span>
                             <span class="n">max_pop_size</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span>
                             <span class="n">res_max_point_size</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">2000</span><span class="p">,</span>
                             <span class="n">job_max_point_size</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">2000</span><span class="p">,</span>
                             <span class="n">green_index</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">,</span>
                             <span class="n">res_cluster_max_pop_threshold</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">,</span>
                             <span class="n">res_cluster_buffer_meters</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">,</span>
                             <span class="n">job_cluster_max_pop_threshold</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">,</span>
                             <span class="n">job_cluster_buffer_meters</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">):</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="sd">"""</span>
<span class="sd">    Cleans up demand's points/pops in place using only data already present -</span>
<span class="sd">    no external stats needed. Mutates and also returns `demand`.</span>

<span class="sd">    `res_cluster_max_pop_threshold`/`res_cluster_buffer_meters` and their</span>
<span class="sd">    `job_` counterparts override the module-level</span>
<span class="sd">    CLUSTER_MAX_POP_THRESHOLD/CLUSTER_BUFFER_METERS defaults passed to</span>
<span class="sd">    depot's cluster_points() - exposed as parameters (rather than just using</span>
<span class="sd">    the module constants directly) so a caller can scale them independently</span>
<span class="sd">    for job vs. residential points (e.g.</span>
<span class="sd">    generate_demand_qzm_local.py's RES_SIZE_RATIO/JOB_SIZE_RATIO) without</span>
<span class="sd">    having to import and mutate the module constants themselves.</span>
<span class="sd">    `agglomerate_small_threshold`/`agglomerate_distance_*` only ever affect</span>
<span class="sd">    residential origin flows (see depot's agglomerate_pops() docstring), so</span>
<span class="sd">    there's no separate job version of those.</span>

<span class="sd">    If `green_index` (a GreenSpaceIndex) is given, it's used twice: right</span>
<span class="sd">    after cluster_points() to merge away any point - including depot's own</span>
<span class="sd">    agglomerate_pops() SO_ centroids, which are plain spatial averages with</span>
<span class="sd">    no awareness of terrain - that landed inside a real green-space polygon</span>
<span class="sd">    into its nearest valid neighbor (see _merge_points_in_green_space()),</span>
<span class="sd">    and again inside enforce_max_point_size() so split siblings don't drift</span>
<span class="sd">    into one either.</span>
<span class="sd">    """</span>
    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"  Merging pops with identical home/work commutes..."</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="n">demand</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">merge_identical_commutes</span><span class="p">()</span>
    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"  -&gt; </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s1">'points'</span><span class="p">])</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> points / </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s1">'pops'</span><span class="p">])</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> pops"</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"  Agglomerating small scattered-origin pops into super-origins..."</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="n">demand</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">agglomerate_pops</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SMALL_THRESHOLD</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">agglomerate_small_threshold</span><span class="p">,</span>
                            <span class="n">DISTANCE_THRESHOLD_NONCBD</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">agglomerate_distance_noncbd</span><span class="p">,</span>
                            <span class="n">DISTANCE_THRESHOLD_CBD</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">agglomerate_distance_cbd</span><span class="p">,</span>
                            <span class="n">cbd_bbox</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">cbd_bbox</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"  -&gt; </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s1">'points'</span><span class="p">])</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> points / </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s1">'pops'</span><span class="p">])</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> pops"</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="c1"># Runs AFTER agglomerate_pops() so it gets the last word over the *whole*</span>
    <span class="c1"># point set, including the new SO_ points agglomerate_pops() just</span>
    <span class="c1"># created - see the module comment above for why the order matters.</span>
    <span class="c1">#</span>
    <span class="c1"># Two SEPARATE passes (job points, then residential points) instead of</span>
    <span class="c1"># one shared call - depot's cluster_points() merges purely by spatial</span>
    <span class="c1"># proximity+size with no awareness of point type, so a single pass can</span>
    <span class="c1"># (and on real data, does) merge a nearby job and residential point into</span>
    <span class="c1"># one mixed blob. Splitting by type is the only way to give job hubs and</span>
    <span class="c1"># residential hubs independent buffer/threshold tuning (see</span>
    <span class="c1"># RES_SIZE_RATIO/JOB_SIZE_RATIO) - as a side effect, job and residential</span>
    <span class="c1"># points can no longer merge into each other at all, which also directly</span>
    <span class="c1"># helps the "too many small scattered job destinations" line-planning</span>
    <span class="c1"># problem this was built for: job points now only ever consolidate with</span>
    <span class="c1"># other job points.</span>
    <span class="n">_prev_verb</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">demand</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">verb</span>
    <span class="n">demand</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">verb</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">True</span>
    <span class="n">job_points</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">[</span><span class="n">p</span> <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">p</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"points"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">_is_job_point</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">p</span><span class="p">)]</span>
    <span class="n">res_points</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">[</span><span class="n">p</span> <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">p</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"points"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="k">if</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="n">_is_job_point</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">p</span><span class="p">)]</span>

    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"  Clustering overlapping job points (</span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">job_points</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2">, Colin's method)..."</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">job_points</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"points"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">job_points</span>
        <span class="n">demand</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cluster_points</span><span class="p">(</span>
            <span class="n">max_pop_threshold</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">job_cluster_max_pop_threshold</span> <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">job_cluster_max_pop_threshold</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="kc">None</span>
                               <span class="k">else</span> <span class="n">CLUSTER_MAX_POP_THRESHOLD</span><span class="p">),</span>
            <span class="n">buffer_meters</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">job_cluster_buffer_meters</span> <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">job_cluster_buffer_meters</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="kc">None</span>
                          <span class="k">else</span> <span class="n">CLUSTER_BUFFER_METERS</span><span class="p">))</span>
        <span class="n">job_points</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"points"</span><span class="p">]</span>
    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"  -&gt; </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">job_points</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> job point(s)"</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"  Clustering overlapping residential points (</span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">res_points</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2">, Colin's method)..."</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">res_points</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"points"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">res_points</span>
        <span class="n">demand</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cluster_points</span><span class="p">(</span>
            <span class="n">max_pop_threshold</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">res_cluster_max_pop_threshold</span> <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">res_cluster_max_pop_threshold</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="kc">None</span>
                               <span class="k">else</span> <span class="n">CLUSTER_MAX_POP_THRESHOLD</span><span class="p">),</span>
            <span class="n">buffer_meters</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">res_cluster_buffer_meters</span> <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">res_cluster_buffer_meters</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="kc">None</span>
                          <span class="k">else</span> <span class="n">CLUSTER_BUFFER_METERS</span><span class="p">))</span>
        <span class="n">res_points</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"points"</span><span class="p">]</span>
    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"  -&gt; </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">res_points</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> residential point(s)"</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"points"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">job_points</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">res_points</span>
    <span class="n">demand</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">verb</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">_prev_verb</span>
    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"  -&gt; </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s1">'points'</span><span class="p">])</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> points / </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s1">'pops'</span><span class="p">])</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> pops"</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">green_index</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="kc">None</span> <span class="ow">and</span> <span class="n">green_index</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">polygons</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"  Merging points that landed inside a green-space polygon into their nearest neighbor..."</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">_merge_points_in_green_space</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">green_index</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"  -&gt; </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s1">'points'</span><span class="p">])</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> points / </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s1">'pops'</span><span class="p">])</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> pops"</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"  Capping pop sizes at </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="n">max_pop_size</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2">..."</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="n">demand</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">enforce_max_pop_size</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">max_pop_size</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"  -&gt; </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s1">'pops'</span><span class="p">])</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> pops"</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"  Capping point sizes at </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="n">res_max_point_size</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> (residential) / </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="n">job_max_point_size</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> (jobs)..."</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="n">enforce_max_point_size</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">res_max_point_size</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">res_max_point_size</span><span class="p">,</span>
                           <span class="n">job_max_point_size</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">job_max_point_size</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">green_index</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">green_index</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"  -&gt; </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s1">'points'</span><span class="p">])</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> points"</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">demand</span>


<span class="c1"># depot's clustering (cluster_points/agglomerate_pops) only ever MERGES</span>
<span class="c1"># points together - there's no equivalent to enforce_max_pop_size() for</span>
<span class="c1"># points, so a genuinely dense area (or the consolidation cluster_and_</span>
<span class="c1"># consolidate() itself just did) can still land as one single giant point.</span>
<span class="c1"># Tightening merge/cluster radii only goes so far: real Berlin data still</span>
<span class="c1"># had 707 points over 2,000 and 10 over 8,000 even at fairly tight settings,</span>
<span class="c1"># because the underlying building-level density is just that high in spots -</span>
<span class="c1"># no merge radius will ever *split* that back apart. This does the splitting</span>
<span class="c1"># ourselves, the same way enforce_max_pop_size() splits an oversized pop into</span>
<span class="c1"># several capped ones.</span>
<span class="n">GOLDEN_ANGLE_RAD</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">pi</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">3</span> <span class="o">-</span> <span class="n">math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">sqrt</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">))</span>  <span class="c1"># ~137.5 deg</span>


<span class="k">class</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">_SpatialIndex</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="sd">"""</span>
<span class="sd">    Simple uniform-grid spatial index (cell size ~= spacing_meters) so</span>
<span class="sd">    "is anything already within spacing_meters of this candidate spot" can be</span>
<span class="sd">    checked in roughly constant time instead of against every point on the</span>
<span class="sd">    whole map. Used so split placement respects points from OTHER splits and</span>
<span class="sd">    pre-existing points too, not just its own siblings - a candidate right</span>
<span class="sd">    next to some unrelated point elsewhere would previously never get</span>
<span class="sd">    rejected.</span>
<span class="sd">    """</span>
    <span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="fm">__init__</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">points</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">spacing_meters</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">ref_lat</span><span class="p">):</span>
        <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cell_deg</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">spacing_meters</span> <span class="o">/</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">111_000</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="nb">max</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cos</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">radians</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ref_lat</span><span class="p">)),</span> <span class="mf">0.1</span><span class="p">))</span>
        <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cells</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{}</span>
        <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">p</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">points</span><span class="p">:</span>
            <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">add</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">p</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"location"</span><span class="p">][</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">],</span> <span class="n">p</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"location"</span><span class="p">][</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">])</span>

    <span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">_key</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">):</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span> <span class="o">/</span> <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cell_deg</span><span class="p">),</span> <span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lat</span> <span class="o">/</span> <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cell_deg</span><span class="p">))</span>

    <span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">add</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">):</span>
        <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cells</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">setdefault</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">_key</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">),</span> <span class="p">[])</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">append</span><span class="p">((</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">))</span>

    <span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">nearest_dist</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">):</span>
        <span class="n">cx</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">cy</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">_key</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">best</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">None</span>
        <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">dx</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">):</span>
            <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">dy</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">):</span>
                <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">olon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">olat</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cells</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">get</span><span class="p">((</span><span class="n">cx</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">dx</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">cy</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">dy</span><span class="p">),</span> <span class="p">[]):</span>
                    <span class="n">d</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">_haversine_m</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">olon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">olat</span><span class="p">)</span>
                    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">best</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="kc">None</span> <span class="ow">or</span> <span class="n">d</span> <span class="o">&lt;</span> <span class="n">best</span><span class="p">:</span>
                        <span class="n">best</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">d</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">best</span>


<span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">_place_split_point</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">index</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">spacing_meters</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">base_lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">base_lat</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">order</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">bbox</span><span class="p">,</span>
                        <span class="n">violations</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">max_attempts</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">green_index</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">,</span>
                        <span class="n">green_corrections</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">):</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="sd">"""</span>
<span class="sd">    Picks a spot for the order-th sibling of a split. order=0 tries the</span>
<span class="sd">    exact original location first (so at least one result stays where the</span>
<span class="sd">    original data actually pointed) - but unlike before, it now actually</span>
<span class="sd">    checks that spot against `index` too instead of returning it</span>
<span class="sd">    unconditionally. That matters once a point gets split a SECOND time</span>
<span class="sd">    (e.g. a landmark's gravity-sampled pops pushed an already-split-once</span>
<span class="sd">    point back over the cap): order=0 there would otherwise reuse a</span>
<span class="sd">    location that's already sitting right next to that point's own pass-1</span>
<span class="sd">    siblings.</span>

<span class="sd">    For every attempt (including a conflicting order=0): the FIRST attempt</span>
<span class="sd">    tries a sqrt(order)-radius golden-angle spiral step (guarantees fresh</span>
<span class="sd">    siblings fan out in different directions from each other rather than</span>
<span class="sd">    clump - see the module note above). If that spot is too close to</span>
<span class="sd">    something, later attempts pick a FULLY random angle (not just a small</span>
<span class="sd">    wobble around that one golden-angle sector) with a radius that grows</span>
<span class="sd">    deterministically each attempt. This is the actual fix for a real bug:</span>
<span class="sd">    the old version only ever wobbled the angle by +-0.6 rad around one</span>
<span class="sd">    fixed sector and grew the radius by a random (not guaranteed-increasing)</span>
<span class="sd">    multiplier - so if that one sector happened to be crowded, every one of</span>
<span class="sd">    its 10 retries could plausibly fail, and it then silently kept the last</span>
<span class="sd">    failed attempt anyway. Verified on real BER data: 465 points ended up</span>
<span class="sd">    within 100m of a neighbor, some as close as 13m, all traced back to this.</span>

<span class="sd">    Checked via `index`, which the caller keeps updated with every point</span>
<span class="sd">    placed so far (siblings AND unrelated points alike). Clamped inside</span>
<span class="sd">    `bbox` ([min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat]) if given, with a small</span>
<span class="sd">    inset so nothing ends up sitting exactly on the map edge.</span>

<span class="sd">    If `green_index` (a GreenSpaceIndex) is given, a candidate landing</span>
<span class="sd">    inside a captured green-space polygon (park/nature_reserve/water_park/</span>
<span class="sd">    etc.) is rejected the same way a too-close spacing violation is -</span>
<span class="sd">    fixes split siblings drifting into a huge, mostly-empty park (e.g.</span>
<span class="sd">    Tempelhofer Feld) since nothing previously checked terrain, only</span>
<span class="sd">    distance to other points.</span>

<span class="sd">    If `violations` (a list) is passed and every attempt still lands within</span>
<span class="sd">    spacing_meters of something (a genuinely saturated area - no amount of</span>
<span class="sd">    retrying will fix that), the least-bad candidate found is used and its</span>
<span class="sd">    clearance distance is appended to `violations` for the caller to</span>
<span class="sd">    summarize, instead of failing/warning per-point.</span>

<span class="sd">    If that final fallback candidate is inside a green-space polygon</span>
<span class="sd">    (rather than just a spacing violation), this returns (None, None)</span>
<span class="sd">    instead of placing anything there, and counts it in `green_corrections`</span>
<span class="sd">    (a list) if given - the caller is expected to fold this sub-point's</span>
<span class="sd">    population into an already-placed sibling instead. An earlier version</span>
<span class="sd">    nudged it to just outside the polygon boundary via</span>
<span class="sd">    GreenSpaceIndex.push_outside(), but for a park with many split siblings</span>
<span class="sd">    all originating nearby, that piles several "corrected" points on top of</span>
<span class="sd">    each other right at the boundary - the same overlapping-clusters</span>
<span class="sd">    problem this was meant to fix, just moved onto the park's edge.</span>
<span class="sd">    """</span>
    <span class="n">lat_scale</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1</span> <span class="o">/</span> <span class="mi">111_000</span>
    <span class="n">lon_scale</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1</span> <span class="o">/</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">111_000</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="nb">max</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cos</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">radians</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">base_lat</span><span class="p">)),</span> <span class="mf">0.1</span><span class="p">))</span>

    <span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">_clamp</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">):</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="n">bbox</span><span class="p">:</span>
            <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span>
        <span class="n">inset</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">spacing_meters</span> <span class="o">/</span> <span class="mi">111_000</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">min</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">max</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">bbox</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">inset</span><span class="p">),</span> <span class="n">bbox</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">-</span> <span class="n">inset</span><span class="p">),</span>
                <span class="nb">min</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">max</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">bbox</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">inset</span><span class="p">),</span> <span class="n">bbox</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">-</span> <span class="n">inset</span><span class="p">))</span>

    <span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">_is_valid</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">):</span>
        <span class="n">nearest</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">index</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">nearest_dist</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">spacing_ok</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">nearest</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="kc">None</span> <span class="ow">or</span> <span class="n">nearest</span> <span class="o">&gt;=</span> <span class="n">spacing_meters</span>
        <span class="n">green_ok</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">green_index</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="kc">None</span> <span class="ow">or</span> <span class="n">green_index</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">containing_polygon</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="kc">None</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">spacing_ok</span> <span class="ow">and</span> <span class="n">green_ok</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">nearest</span>

    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">order</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">_clamp</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">base_lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">base_lat</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">ok</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">_</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">_is_valid</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">ok</span><span class="p">:</span>
            <span class="n">index</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">add</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">)</span>
            <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span>
        <span class="c1"># Falls through to the same randomized search below instead of</span>
        <span class="c1"># blindly keeping a spot already known to violate spacing or land</span>
        <span class="c1"># inside a green-space polygon.</span>

    <span class="n">best</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">None</span>  <span class="c1"># (nearest_dist_or_inf, lon, lat) - kept in case every attempt fails</span>
    <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">attempt</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="nb">range</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">max_attempts</span><span class="p">):</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">attempt</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">:</span>
            <span class="n">theta</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">order</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">GOLDEN_ANGLE_RAD</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">random</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">uniform</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mf">0.3</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mf">0.3</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="k">else</span><span class="p">:</span>
            <span class="n">theta</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">random</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">uniform</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">2</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">pi</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">radius</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">spacing_meters</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">sqrt</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">max</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">order</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">))</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="mf">1.0</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">attempt</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="mf">0.3</span><span class="p">)</span>

        <span class="n">lon</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">base_lon</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">radius</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cos</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">theta</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">lon_scale</span>
        <span class="n">lat</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">base_lat</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">radius</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">sin</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">theta</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">lat_scale</span>
        <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">_clamp</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">)</span>

        <span class="n">ok</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">nearest</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">_is_valid</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">ok</span><span class="p">:</span>
            <span class="n">index</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">add</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">)</span>
            <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span>
        <span class="c1"># Tracked purely by spacing clearance (None/large is "best") - a</span>
        <span class="c1"># rejection caused only by green-space with otherwise perfect</span>
        <span class="c1"># spacing gets corrected below regardless of which check failed.</span>
        <span class="n">clearance</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">nearest</span> <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">nearest</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="kc">None</span> <span class="k">else</span> <span class="nb">float</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s1">'inf'</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">best</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="kc">None</span> <span class="ow">or</span> <span class="n">clearance</span> <span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">best</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]:</span>
            <span class="n">best</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="n">clearance</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="n">clearance</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">best</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">green_index</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="kc">None</span> <span class="ow">and</span> <span class="n">green_index</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">containing_polygon</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="c1"># Every attempt landed either too close to another point or inside</span>
        <span class="c1"># green space, and this final fallback candidate is itself still</span>
        <span class="c1"># inside a green-space polygon - don't place anything here at all;</span>
        <span class="c1"># signal the caller to fold this sub-point into an already-placed</span>
        <span class="c1"># sibling instead (see the docstring above for why).</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">green_corrections</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">:</span>
            <span class="n">green_corrections</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">append</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="kc">None</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">violations</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="kc">None</span> <span class="ow">and</span> <span class="n">clearance</span> <span class="o">&lt;</span> <span class="n">spacing_meters</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="n">violations</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">append</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">clearance</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="n">index</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">add</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span>


<span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">_merge_points_in_green_space</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">green_index</span><span class="p">):</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="sd">"""</span>
<span class="sd">    Scans every ordinary (non-special-demand) point and, for any that land</span>
<span class="sd">    inside a captured green-space polygon, removes it and folds its</span>
<span class="sd">    residents/jobs (and every pop referencing it) into its nearest</span>
<span class="sd">    still-valid neighbor instead. This is the sweep that catches what the</span>
<span class="sd">    OSM-extraction edge-push (_green_space_edge_location()) and split</span>
<span class="sd">    placement (_place_split_point()'s green_index check) can't: depot's own</span>
<span class="sd">    agglomerate_pops() computes each new SO_ point's location as a plain</span>
<span class="sd">    spatial centroid of the residences it groups, with no awareness of</span>
<span class="sd">    terrain, so it can place a point in the middle of a large, mostly-empty</span>
<span class="sd">    park (e.g. Tempelhofer Feld) even though none of the actual residences</span>
<span class="sd">    that fed into it are there. Runs once, right after cluster_points()</span>
<span class="sd">    settles - the last point in the pipeline where depot's own code still</span>
<span class="sd">    has a chance to create such a point.</span>

<span class="sd">    An earlier version of this NUDGED the offending point to just outside</span>
<span class="sd">    the polygon boundary instead of merging it away. That's fine for one</span>
<span class="sd">    stray point, but a big, mostly-empty park can have MANY SO_ centroids</span>
<span class="sd">    scattered across it - nudging every one of them lands most at roughly</span>
<span class="sd">    the same nearest edge spot, reproducing the exact overlapping-clusters</span>
<span class="sd">    look this was supposed to fix, just now sitting on the park boundary</span>
<span class="sd">    instead of inside it. Merging into whatever real point already exists</span>
<span class="sd">    nearby (a building/hub that was always going to be there) doesn't</span>
<span class="sd">    create anything new at the boundary at all.</span>

<span class="sd">    Nearest-neighbor lookup uses a cKDTree over every still-valid ORDINARY</span>
<span class="sd">    point's location (same tool already used elsewhere in this codebase for</span>
<span class="sd">    cluster_organic()) rather than a linear scan, since a big city can have</span>
<span class="sd">    tens of thousands of points.</span>

<span class="sd">    Special demand points are never removed (same reasoning as</span>
<span class="sd">    enforce_max_point_size()) AND never used as a merge target either - a</span>
<span class="sd">    landmark's total_capacity is a real, researched number (see</span>
<span class="sd">    add_named_special_demand()'s docstring on why that number must stay</span>
<span class="sd">    exact), and a landmark can legitimately sit inside a park's boundary in</span>
<span class="sd">    real life (e.g. the church actually located on Tempelhofer Feld) without</span>
<span class="sd">    that meaning ordinary residential/job capacity should get folded onto</span>
<span class="sd">    it. Mutates and returns `demand`.</span>
<span class="sd">    """</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">green_index</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="kc">None</span> <span class="ow">or</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="n">green_index</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">polygons</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">demand</span>

    <span class="n">points</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"points"</span><span class="p">]</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="n">points</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">demand</span>

    <span class="n">special_prefixes</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nb">set</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">special_demand_ids</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">keys</span><span class="p">())</span>
    <span class="n">merge_targets</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">[]</span>  <span class="c1"># ordinary, non-green points only - eligible to receive merged capacity</span>
    <span class="n">bad_points</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">[]</span>
    <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">point</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">points</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="n">prefix</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">point</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"id"</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">split</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"_"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">)[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">prefix</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">special_prefixes</span><span class="p">:</span>
            <span class="k">continue</span>  <span class="c1"># never removed, never merged into - left in demand["points"] untouched</span>
        <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">point</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"location"</span><span class="p">]</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">green_index</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">containing_polygon</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">:</span>
            <span class="n">merge_targets</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">append</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">point</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="k">else</span><span class="p">:</span>
            <span class="n">bad_points</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">append</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">point</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="n">bad_points</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">demand</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="n">merge_targets</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="c1"># No ordinary point anywhere to merge into (degenerate case) - leave</span>
        <span class="c1"># these as-is rather than inflating a special-demand landmark's</span>
        <span class="c1"># researched capacity number by merging into it instead.</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">demand</span>

    <span class="c1"># (lat, lon) ordering, matching cluster_organic()'s existing cKDTree</span>
    <span class="c1"># convention elsewhere in this file.</span>
    <span class="n">valid_coords</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">array</span><span class="p">([[</span><span class="n">p</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"location"</span><span class="p">][</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">],</span> <span class="n">p</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"location"</span><span class="p">][</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]]</span> <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">p</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">merge_targets</span><span class="p">])</span>
    <span class="n">tree</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">cKDTree</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">valid_coords</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="n">pops_by_id</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span><span class="n">p</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"id"</span><span class="p">]:</span> <span class="n">p</span> <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">p</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"pops"</span><span class="p">]}</span>
    <span class="n">merged_residents</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span>
    <span class="n">merged_jobs</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span>
    <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">bad_point</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">bad_points</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lat</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">bad_point</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"location"</span><span class="p">]</span>
        <span class="n">_</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">idx</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">tree</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">query</span><span class="p">((</span><span class="n">lat</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lon</span><span class="p">))</span>
        <span class="n">target</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">merge_targets</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span>

        <span class="n">target</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"residents"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">+=</span> <span class="n">bad_point</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"residents"</span><span class="p">]</span>
        <span class="n">target</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"jobs"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">+=</span> <span class="n">bad_point</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"jobs"</span><span class="p">]</span>
        <span class="n">merged_residents</span> <span class="o">+=</span> <span class="n">bad_point</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"residents"</span><span class="p">]</span>
        <span class="n">merged_jobs</span> <span class="o">+=</span> <span class="n">bad_point</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"jobs"</span><span class="p">]</span>

        <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">pop_id</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">bad_point</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"popIds"</span><span class="p">]:</span>
            <span class="n">pop</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">pops_by_id</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">get</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">pop_id</span><span class="p">)</span>
            <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">pop</span> <span class="ow">is</span> <span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">:</span>
                <span class="k">continue</span>
            <span class="c1"># A pop can reference this point as BOTH residenceId and jobId</span>
            <span class="c1"># (a self-loop pop from depot's own cluster_points() merging a</span>
            <span class="c1"># residential and job point together) - handle each role</span>
            <span class="c1"># independently, same pattern as enforce_max_point_size()/</span>
            <span class="c1"># _clear_ordinary_points_within(). Checked against the pop's</span>
            <span class="c1"># CURRENT value (not a cached copy) so a pop whose OTHER</span>
            <span class="c1"># endpoint is also a bad point being merged in this same pass</span>
            <span class="c1"># still ends up correctly pointing at both merge targets.</span>
            <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">pop</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"residenceId"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="n">bad_point</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"id"</span><span class="p">]:</span>
                <span class="n">pop</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"residenceId"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">target</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"id"</span><span class="p">]</span>
            <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">pop</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"jobId"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="n">bad_point</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"id"</span><span class="p">]:</span>
                <span class="n">pop</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"jobId"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">target</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"id"</span><span class="p">]</span>
            <span class="n">target</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"popIds"</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">append</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">pop_id</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="n">bad_ids</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span><span class="n">p</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"id"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">p</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">bad_points</span><span class="p">}</span>
    <span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"points"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">[</span><span class="n">p</span> <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">p</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">points</span> <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">p</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"id"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">bad_ids</span><span class="p">]</span>

    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"  -&gt; Merged </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">bad_points</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> point(s) that landed inside a "</span>
          <span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"green-space polygon (</span><span class="si">{</span><span class="n">merged_residents</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> residents / "</span>
          <span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="si">{</span><span class="n">merged_jobs</span><span class="si">:</span><span class="s2">,</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2"> jobs) into their nearest still-valid neighbor, "</span>
          <span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"instead of relocating them onto the park boundary."</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">demand</span>


<span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">enforce_max_point_size</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">demand</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">res_max_point_size</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">2000</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">job_max_point_size</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">2000</span><span class="p">,</span>
                           <span class="n">spacing_meters</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">250</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">green_index</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">):</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="sd">"""</span>
<span class="sd">    Splits any ordinary (non-special-demand) point whose residents+jobs</span>
<span class="sd">    total exceeds its applicable cap into multiple smaller points, each</span>
